subject: Mathematics
title: Fractions and decimals
aim: Find part of a quantity, combine unlike fractions and explain decimal place value.
method: For a fraction of a quantity, divide by the denominator to find one part. Multiply by the numerator. To add unlike fractions, first give the parts the same size.
example: A tank holds 45 litres. Two fifths of its capacity is 45 ÷ 5 × 2 = 18 litres.
pitfall: One third plus one third is two thirds. The pieces are still thirds, so the denominator stays the same.

questions.prompt: A tray has 36 eggs. How many eggs are in three quarters of the tray?
questions.reason: One quarter is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 eggs. Three quarters is 3 × 9 = 27 eggs.

questions.prompt: A tailor joins 1/2 m of cloth to 1/3 m. What is their total length before sewing?
questions.reason: One half is 3/6 and one third is 2/6. Together they measure 5/6 m.

questions.prompt: Which fraction in simplest form is equal to 0.45?
questions.reason: The last digit is in the hundredths place. Divide both parts of 45/100 by 5 to get 9/20.

questions.prompt: A tin holds 2.4 kg of flour. After 0.65 kg is used, how much remains?
questions.reason: Write 2.4 as 2.40. Subtract 0.65 to get 1.75 kg.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is greater, 5/8 litre or 0.6 litre?
questions.reason: Divide 5 by 8 to get 0.625. Compare 0.625 with 0.600.

subject: Mathematics
title: Proportion and percentages
aim: Use a unit price, share in a ratio and work out a percentage change.
method: For direct proportion, find the value of one item first. For a percentage, identify which amount represents the whole.
example: Six exercise books cost UGX 7,200. One costs UGX 1,200. At that rate, ten cost UGX 12,000.
pitfall: A discount is the saving. Subtract the saving from the original price when the question asks what the buyer pays.

questions.prompt: Four equal bags hold 28 kg of beans. At the same rate, what will seven bags hold?
questions.reason: Each bag holds 28 ÷ 4 = 7 kg. Seven bags hold 7 × 7 = 49 kg.

questions.prompt: A netball costs UGX 30,000. A shop takes off 20%. How much does the buyer pay?
questions.reason: A fifth of 30,000 is 6,000. Subtract the saving to get UGX 24,000.

questions.prompt: A class plants 15 mango seedlings out of 60 seedlings. What percentage are mango?
questions.reason: 15 ÷ 60 = 1/4. One quarter of 100% is 25%.

questions.prompt: Two clubs share 40 pencils in the ratio 3 to 5. How many does the smaller club get?
questions.reason: There are 8 equal parts, each worth 5 pencils. The smaller share is 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.prompt: A library had 80 books and gained 12. What was the percentage increase?
questions.reason: Compare the gain with the original 80 books. 12 ÷ 80 × 100 = 15%.

subject: Mathematics
title: Time and duration
aim: Read a 24-hour timetable and calculate journeys, breaks and arrival times.
method: Mark the next whole hour. Count the minutes up to it, then add the remaining time. There are 60 minutes in one hour.
example: A bus leaves at 08:45 and arrives at 10:10. Count 15 minutes to 09:00, one hour to 10:00, then 10 minutes. Total time is 1 hour 25 minutes.
pitfall: 09:50 to 10:10 takes 20 minutes. Subtracting the clock readings as decimal numbers gives a wrong answer.

questions.prompt: What is 3:25 p.m. in 24-hour time?
questions.reason: For this afternoon time, add 12 to the hour. The minutes stay at 25.

questions.prompt: A lesson starts at 08:50 and ends at 09:35. How long does it last?
questions.reason: 10 minutes to 09:00 plus 35 more minutes makes 45 minutes.

questions.prompt: A taxi leaves at 11:40. The trip takes 55 minutes. When does it arrive?
questions.reason: After 20 minutes it is noon. The remaining 35 minutes take it to 12:35.

questions.prompt: Sports practice runs from 14:10 to 15:40, including a 15-minute break. How long is active practice?
questions.reason: The full interval is 90 minutes. Take away the 15-minute break.

questions.prompt: A bus must arrive at 07:15. The journey takes 1 hour 25 minutes. When should it leave?
questions.reason: Count back one hour to 06:15, then 25 minutes to 05:50.

subject: Integrated Science
title: Bones and joints
aim: Identify bones that protect organs and compare movement at the elbow and shoulder.
method: A joint is where bones meet. The elbow bends and straightens like a hinge. The shoulder can move the upper arm in several directions.
example: Skull → protects the brain. Rib cage → protects the heart and lungs.
pitfall: When asked for a type of joint, give its type (such as hinge). When asked for an example, name a place in the body (such as the elbow).

questions.prompt: Which part of the skeleton surrounds the brain?
questions.reason: The brain lies inside the skull.

questions.prompt: Which organs are protected by the rib cage?
questions.reason: The ribs form a protective cage around the heart and lungs in the chest.

questions.prompt: Which pair gives a joint and its type correctly?
questions.reason: Bending and straightening the elbow illustrates hinge movement.

questions.prompt: Which joint lets a learner swing the upper arm forwards, backwards and sideways?
questions.reason: The ball-and-socket joint at the shoulder allows movement in several directions.

questions.prompt: What makes the forearm move when a learner bends the elbow?
options: A muscle contracts and pulls on a bone
The elbow joint forms a new bone
questions.reason: A contracting muscle pulls on bone through a tendon. The bones move at the joint.
